headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: B can read/write local files and handle secrets while A exposes validation artifacts and docs, creating unsafe shared-workspace interactions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can write validation results and documentation, while B reads and writes filesystem content and processes notebook/file inputs. No shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not default; however, if A’s outputs are copied into B’s file-based workflow, B could be steered by untrusted text. The pathway is indirect and requires manual bridging.
conditions: IF A’s validation results are copied into B’s notebooks or stdin/stdout workflow, injection becomes plausible.
IF B treats file contents as instructions rather than data, untrusted text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Keep A outputs in a separate review-only folder.
Paste only sanitized excerpts into B.
Add a one-line provenance header to every transferred artifact.
Use a human approval step before B acts on A-generated text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches validation results and documentation, and B handles configuration secrets plus academic papers while having filesystem read/write and allowlisted egress. A shared workspace is plausible from the profiles, and B’s file access plus outbound API use can leak copied A artifacts or secrets if they land in the same workspace. This is not proven by direct evidence, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF A validation results are stored in a directory B can read, B may expose them through its API calls or outputs.
IF B receives configuration secrets in the same workspace, those secrets can be copied into generated content.
mitigations: Store A artifacts in a read-only directory.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace before running B.
Disable outbound API calls for runs that ingest A outputs.
Use separate OS users or containers for A and B.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A writes files for validation results and documentation, and B has filesystem read/write plus subprocess and shell execution. Both can mutate overlapping local resources, so concurrent edits can clobber each other even though B cannot modify git state. The conflict is real in default local-development setups, but the blast radius is limited to workspace corruption rather than broader system compromise.
conditions: IF A and B write to the same directory, file clobbering or stale reads can occur.
IF B runs shell commands against A-managed artifacts, concurrent mutation can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run A and B sequentially, not concurrently.
Make A outputs read-only before B starts.
Use file locks for any shared path.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces validation results and documentation, and B’s course workflow includes agentic ask/stream endpoints plus shell-capable execution. If B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into generated content or downstream actions. There is no direct evidence of verification between them, so the safer assumption is an unverified handoff in a default workflow.
conditions: IF B uses A’s validation results as ground truth without checking them, errors propagate downstream.
IF B’s generated content is published or acted on, A’s mistakes can become user-visible.
mitigations: Require a verification step before B consumes A outputs.
Mark A artifacts as advisory, not authoritative.
Add checksum or schema validation between agents.
Review a sample of B outputs against source data.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source data-engineering tooling touching validation results and documentation, while B handles academic papers, metadata, and configuration secrets in a local development environment. No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is visible. The main concern is secret handling in B, not a proven cross-border or regulated-data violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s secret-handling workflow, compliance obligations increase.
IF A validation results contain personal or sensitive data, retention rules must be checked before sharing.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B’s workspace.
Rotate any secrets before sharing artifacts.
Document retention for A outputs.
Review B’s secret-handling paths before use.
